transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in today?

I’m just tired all the time and don’t have the energy to do much of anything anymore, even the stuff I used to enjoy. It feels like I'm just going through the motions every day, and I can't seem to shake this constant exhaustion.
Have you lost interest in activities you used to enjoy, or do they no longer bring you pleasure?

Yes, absolutely. Things I used to love, like fishing, working on vintage hardware, or volunteering with the youth robotics club, now just feel like chores I have to push myself through. Even when I'm doing those things or sitting with my grandkids, this gray cloud hangs over me and I catch myself thinking, "what's the point?"
Have you been feeling down or depressed most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks?

Yes, I have. It's like a low, gray cloud hanging over me most days, where nothing feels worth getting excited about anymore. But this has been going on for much longer than two weeks—it has actually been a constant feeling for a couple of years now, ever since I started transitioning into retirement.

Have you had any periods lasting several months or longer where you felt significantly better—where your mood improved and you regained interest in activities—for at least two consecutive months before this current episode?

No, I haven't had any breaks like that at all. Once this low, worn-out feeling settled in after I started retiring over two years ago, it has pretty much stuck with me constantly. I haven't had any periods where I felt like my old self or got my energy back.

latest_inference.note: Previously the candidates were [F32, F33], with F32 (episodic depressive disorder) considered due to the presence of a current depressive episode. However, the patient reports that the low mood has been present constantly for over two years without any remission of at least two months, which rules out F32, as it requires a single or multiple discrete episodes separated by full recovery. The chronic, uninterrupted course since retirement aligns with recurrent depressive disorder, current episode prolonged, making F33 the only remaining candidate.
